reading.body:
CyrusOne Lebanon, OH publishes 12 MW of IT capacity, the largest among Ohio data centers that report power, yet this is modest against the multi-hundred-megawatt clusters AI scaling now demands.

At 40 kW per rack, 12 MW supports roughly 300 racks across 400,000 square feet. That scale places it first in Ohio, where it accounts for 20 percent of the state's 60.4 MW of published data center IT load across 77 mapped facilities, but Ohio's total remains small relative to major AI buildouts.

The facility's certifications cover SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16, and Green Globes, qualifying it for regulated enterprise workloads rather than signaling AI-specific capability. No tenant, pricing, grid connection, or announced expansion information is published, so whether this site can grow into the sustained high-density load AI infrastructure requires remains unknown.
